summary.text: An invertible matrix is a square matrix that has an inverse, so multiplying the two together gives the identity matrix.
Applying a matrix to a vector and then its inverse returns the original vector, because the inverse undoes the operation.
A square matrix is invertible exactly when its determinant is nonzero, while a matrix with determinant zero collapses volume to zero and has no inverse.

facts.label: Without an inverse
facts.value: A square matrix like that is called singular or degenerate

facts.label: Finding the inverse
facts.value: Row-reduce the matrix beside the identity matrix

facts.label: Notation
facts.value: The inverse of A is written A⁻¹

facts.label: Rank test
facts.value: An n × n matrix with rank n is invertible

items.prompt: A matrix transforms a vector into a new vector. Which matrix brings back the original vector?

options.label: Its inverse
The same matrix applied again
A matrix filled with zeros
Its determinant

items.explain: If a matrix is applied to a vector, followed by applying its inverse, the result is the original vector.

items.prompt: A matrix squashes every three-dimensional shape into a flat sheet with no volume. What does this say about it?

options.label: It is invertible, with a large determinant
It is invertible, because nothing is lost
It is not invertible, since its determinant is zero
It must be the identity matrix

items.explain: A matrix with determinant zero collapses volume to zero and is not invertible; an invertible matrix does not collapse space.

items.prompt: Can a matrix with 3 rows and 5 columns be invertible?

options.label: Yes, if all its entries are nonzero
No, only square matrices have inverses
Yes, with a 5 by 3 inverse
Yes, if its determinant is one

items.explain: An invertible matrix is a square matrix that has an inverse of the same size, so a matrix that is not square cannot qualify.

items.prompt: To find an inverse by hand, you write the matrix next to a second block and row-reduce. What goes in the second block, and what happens?

options.label: A zero matrix; the left side becomes zeros
A copy of the matrix; both sides become equal
Its determinant; the left side becomes a number
The identity matrix; the right side becomes the inverse

items.explain: Gaussian elimination converts the left side into the identity matrix, which causes the right side to become the inverse of the input matrix.

items.prompt: What is a square matrix without an inverse called?

options.label: Regular
Singular
Non-singular
Involutory

items.explain: Over a field, a square matrix that is not invertible is called singular or degenerate.

items.prompt: A 4 × 4 matrix has rank 4. What does that tell you about it?

options.label: It must be the identity matrix
Its determinant must be zero
It has an inverse
It collapses space to a flat set

items.explain: An n × n matrix whose rank is n is of full rank, and such a matrix is invertible.
